title.narrative: Peru First Progrmmatic Environmental Development Policy Loan /DDO

description.narrative: The Environmental Development Policy Loan Program (ENVDPL) aims at supporting the government's efforts to strengthen environmental governance and institutions in Peru, and mainstream environmental sustainability in the development agenda of key sectors (mining, fisheries, and urban transport and energy). The ENVDPL promotes improvements in health particularly of the poor who are exposed to the highest risks from environmental degradation. The ENVDPL is consistent with one of the key pillars of the 2006 Country Partnership Strategy (CPS) for Peru for FY07-FY11 (and the 2009 CPS progress report) laying out a strategy to support the Government of Peru (GoP) to achieve its goals of sustained economic growth. The CPS recognizes the need to raise the profile of environmental issues in Peru by enhancing environmental public investments and strengthening the institutional framework. In support of the CPS' pillar on economic growth, the ENVDPL program will contribute to making growth environmentally sustainable by supporting the environmental legal and institutional framework, biodiversity conservation, enhancing control over air and water pollution, improving the sustainability of the mining sector and the sustainable management of fisheries resources. In addition, by supporting the policy instruments of the newly created Ministry of Environment (MINAM), the ENVDPL would contribute to the modernization of the state institutions.

title.narrative: Air quality data for the Lima-Callao Metropolitan Region is widely published and disseminated (in real time).

baseline.value: Data were not disseminated in real time

target.value: Data are disseminated in real time

actual.value: Data is disseminated on-line with some delay.

title.narrative: Air quality contingency plans are developed.

baseline.value: Pollution contingency plans do not exist in Peru, except in La Oroya

target.value: Air quality contingency plans area developed and implemented in the 5 most polluted cities: Lima, Arequipa, Chimbote, Ilo and LaOroya.

actual.value: Air quality action plans have been prepared in 5 cities. The plans outline actions to be considered during contingencies. However,Peru does not have operational air quality contingency plans.

comment.narrative: Lima and Callao have action plans. Similar instruments (titled "action plans") have been implemented in Arequipa, Chimbote, Ilo andLa Oroya.

title.narrative: Number of environmental participatory monitoring projects in the mining sector.

target.value: Environmental participatory monitoring undertaken in at least 60 sites.

actual.value: Environmental participatory monitoring undertaken in more than 60 sites.

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Energy and Mines reviewed all Environmental Management Instruments registered between 2008 and 2012. Out of 208instruments, 24 instruments established committees and 77 included programs aimed at environmental participatory monitoring. Otherinstruments opted for establishing Permanent Information Office.

title.narrative: Number of vehicles converted to natural gas and number of service stations supplying natural gas in Lima.

baseline.value: 35,000 vehicles converted to NG in Lima.

target.value: At least 80,000 vehicles converted to natural gas (NG) and 90 service stations are installed and operating in Lima.

actual.value: In the metropolitan area of Lima-Callao, more than 162,000,000 vehicles and 1,000 buses have been converted to natural gas. Thenumber of service stations providing natural gas in the country increased to 245 in the country. The Metropolitan Area Lima-Callaohas more than 90 service stations providing natural gas.

title.narrative: Vehicle inspection and maintenance system operating in Lima.

baseline.value: 6 inspection lanes operational in Lima for heavy-duty vehicles.

target.value: Vehicle inspection and maintenance system operating in Lima (with at least 600,000 vehicles inspected), and in each of the 3largest cities (with at least 80,000 vehicles inspected).

actual.value: Currently more than 1,000,000 vehicles are inspected yearly in 7 inspection centers in Lima, and 7 inspection centers in Callao.Cities such as Arequipa, Trujillo, Chiclayo, and Cusco count with vehicle inspection centers.

comment.narrative: Each inspection center has 2 or 3 lanes.

title.narrative: Number of EIAs of large infrastructure/investment projects with potentially significant impacts reviewed by MINAM.

baseline.value: INRENA reviewed 77 EIAs for projects (large and small) which could have an impact on natural resources

target.value: MINAM will review at least 10 EIAs of infrastructure/investment projects with potentially significant impacts.

actual.value: In 2011, MINAM reviewed a sample of 200 EIAs for investment projects with potentially significant impacts. By 2011 MINAM hadachieved the end target.

comment.narrative: In addition, the director of SENACE - the new agency of MINAM which will review detailed EIAs - was selected in February, 2014.

title.narrative: Priority MELs are identified following the priority setting update of MELs inventory and resources for remediating priority public/private MELs confirmed.

baseline.value: No MELs have been identified using technical criteria, and resources have not been confirmed for public/private MEL remediation.

target.value: At least 10 priority MELs are identified following the priority setting update of MELs inventory and resources for remediatingpriority public/private MELS have confirmed resources.

actual.value: To date the updated inventory includes 8616 MELs. The inventory is published on the website of the Ministry of Energy & Mines.Since 2010, 119 MELs in priority areas of Cajamarca and 755 other legacies in 21 former mining units have been remediated throughthe state-owned agency, Activos Mineros.

title.narrative: Increased NPA funding from various sources (including private sector) by at least US$ 2 million per year.

baseline.value: Resource allocation from various sources to the National System of Natural Protected Areas (SINANPE) of US$14.2 million.

actual.value: In 2014 and 2015, resource allocation to SERNAP amounted to more than US$ 17 million per year.

title.narrative: Percentage of anchoveta fleet under the quota system.

target.value: 100 percent of anchoveta fleet under the quota system.

actual.value: Less than 100 percent of anchoveta fleet is under the quota system

title.narrative: Gas stations supplying diesel in Lima supply 50ppm diesel.

target.value: At least 30 percent of gas stations in main cities (approx. 750) supplying clean diesel (with less than 50 ppm of sulfur content)by 2010.

actual.value: All gas stations in the metropolitan area Lima-Callao (more than 750) supply diesel with less than 50 ppm of sulfur. Gas stationsin four additional cities/departments supply diesel with less than 50 ppm: Madre de Dios, Puno, Arequipa, and Moquegua.

comment.narrative: Gas stations in other 4 cities/departments (Madre Dios, Puno, Arequipa, Moquegua) supply diesel with less than 50 ppm

title.narrative: Number of workers take advantage of economic incentives for leaving the fisheries sector.

target.value: At least 3000 workers benefit from economic incentives for leaving the sector.

actual.value: 2,046 workers benefited from economic incentives for leaving the sector

comment.narrative: Out of 2.275 workers who left the fisheries sector, 2,049 applied and received the benefit. The deadline for applying forthe benefits ended in December, 2012.
